source.experiment: GPT reconstruction of fixed-2026-only all-k outer diagnostics using nested_validation.py fit/predict functions

bootstrap.pairing: k=6 and k=10 use the same sampled date clusters in every replicate
bootstrap.clusterPreservation: all matches and both team-side rows for each sampled date are retained together
bootstrap.statistic: D = score(k=6) - score(k=10); D < 0 favors k=6
bootstrap.brierDefinition: mean over team-side targets of the sum of four squared one-hot probability errors
bootstrap.logLossDefinition: mean negative log probability of the observed 0/1/2/3+ category; probability floor 1e-12

interpretation.conclusion: No statistically established superiority of k=6 over k=10 in this retrospective 17-date cluster sensitivity analysis.
interpretation.deploymentDecision: Do not change production model or market weights; k=10 remains the research baseline and k=6 remains a candidate.
interpretation.scope: Retrospective date-cluster sensitivity only; not the prospective round-level primary analysis.

limitations: The 17 target dates do not carry official toto round IDs, so a round-cluster primary analysis is not computed here.
The source history snapshot contains 429 rows with one shared fetchedAt timestamp; this is not match-specific first-observed provenance.
The team alias map was last updated 2026-10-22; 12 of the 17 target dates precede that alias-map update.
The result evaluates frozen predictions from the pinned all-k artifact; it does not regenerate the nested model or establish prospective performance.
